# Sheep casings

<!-- BEGIN: hmi-opening -->
<div class="hmi-quick-read">
  <div class="hmi-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>
  <p>Lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury in sheep casings are reported as monitoring results, studies, references by form and basis, limits, testing and controls.</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Metals of concern:</strong> the metals named by the studies cited on this page.</li>
    <li><strong>Main drivers:</strong> form, origin and preparation stay separate.</li>
    <li><strong>Practical framing:</strong> this page does not pool those studies into one typical value.</li>
  </ul>
</div>

This page draws on 1 peer-reviewed study. The complete citation list is at the bottom of the page.
<!-- END: hmi-opening -->

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="sheep-casings-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="sheep-casings-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="sheep-casings-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Sheep casings in the HMI library has 63 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury from 1 source.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wysok B, Wojtacka J, Szczotka-Bochniarz A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Heavy Metal Contamination in Natural Sheep Casings</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals measured:</strong>

Lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury, in 63 results from 1 source.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wysok B, Wojtacka J, Szczotka-Bochniarz A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Heavy Metal Contamination in Natural Sheep Casings</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Form, basis and where the sheep casings was sampled; reporting limits decide how many results are non-detects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wysok B, Wojtacka J, Szczotka-Bochniarz A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Heavy Metal Contamination in Natural Sheep Casings</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot results with a quantification limit well below the limit that applies in the destination market.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wysok B, Wojtacka J, Szczotka-Bochniarz A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Heavy Metal Contamination in Natural Sheep Casings</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
</ul>
</section>

<a id="decision-summary"></a>
## Sheep casings overview

<a id="hmi-ing-004"></a>
<a id="which-contamination-concerns-are-supported-for-this-ingredient-and-its-defined-forms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-005"></a>
<a id="which-sourcing-or-production-decisions-deserve-priority-on-the-available-evidence"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-006"></a>
<a id="which-evidence-gaps-most-limit-those-decisions"></a>

Sheep casings in the HMI library has 63 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury from 1 source.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wysok B, Wojtacka J, Szczotka-Bochniarz A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Heavy Metal Contamination in Natural Sheep Casings</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Wysok et al. 2025 reported lead at 77 µg/kg (mean ± 45 SD), cadmium at 9 µg/kg (mean ± 8 SD) and total arsenic at 36 µg/kg (mean ± 29 SD) in sheep casings, as sold from all samples (8 countries).<sup class="cite">[[sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wysok B, Wojtacka J, Szczotka-Bochniarz A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Heavy Metal Contamination in Natural Sheep Casings</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the sheep casings came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as sheep casings

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers sheep casings, as sold (63 results).<sup class="cite">[[sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wysok B, Wojtacka J, Szczotka-Bochniarz A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Heavy Metal Contamination in Natural Sheep Casings</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Results stay on the basis each source reports: as sold or fresh weight, dry weight, or unstated. Dry-weight, as-sold and unstated results are never pooled, and no moisture conversion is applied.

<a id="heavy-metal-contamination-profile"></a>
## Heavy metal contamination profile of sheep casings

<a id="hmi-ing-007"></a>
<a id="which-metals-and-chemical-species-have-been-investigated-in-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-008"></a>
<a id="what-concentrations-detection-frequencies-and-variability-were-observed-in-each-defined-sampling-frame"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-009"></a>
<a id="which-analyte-questions-are-unassessed-access-blocked-conflicting-or-searched-without-eligible-evidence"></a>

The table holds every extracted sheep casings result: one row for each statistic a source reports for a form, group and metal, 63 rows in all, grouped by metal and form; percentiles, ranges and maxima for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wysok B, Wojtacka J, Szczotka-Bochniarz A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Heavy Metal Contamination in Natural Sheep Casings</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Monitoring medians are HMI calculations from individual submissions; non-detects remain intervals between zero and the reporting limit and are never read as zero.

0 rows can be rated against an HMI reference for the same form and basis, 24 rows have a direct same-study comparison, and the rest stay unrated with the reason recorded. 1 value from 1 source failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wysok B, Wojtacka J, Szczotka-Bochniarz A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Heavy Metal Contamination in Natural Sheep Casings</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-sheep-casings" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-sheep-casings-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of sheep casings, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>Wysok et al. 2025 is the only compatible sampling family for sheep casings, as sold on this basis in the completed sheep casings ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings" class="internal" data-slug="sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings" data-no-cite-meta>Wysok et al. 2025</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach sheep casings

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

No study in the library compared sheep casings from contaminated and ordinary settings, so the routes by which metals reach it are not measured here.

<a id="ranges-by-source-region-and-variety"></a>
## Which forms and regions measured lower

<a id="hmi-ing-013"></a>
<a id="how-do-concentrations-vary-by-origin-growing-conditions-variety-and-harvest-period"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-014"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-distinguishes-within-lot-between-lot-supplier-and-production-system-variation"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-015"></a>
<a id="which-comparisons-support-a-sourcing-decision-and-where-would-geographic-or-supplier-generalization-be-unjustified"></a>

The HMI reference for total mercury in sheep casings, as sold pools 9 subgroup units from 1 sampling family, with a median of below 1 µg/kg and a middle half spanning below 1 (lower quartile) and below 1 µg/kg (upper quartile).<sup class="cite">[[sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wysok B, Wojtacka J, Szczotka-Bochniarz A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Heavy Metal Contamination in Natural Sheep Casings</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

In one study, lead across 8 groups of sheep casings ranged from 64 µg/kg (casings of New Zealand origin) to 97 µg/kg (casings of Pakistan origin); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wysok B, Wojtacka J, Szczotka-Bochniarz A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Heavy Metal Contamination in Natural Sheep Casings</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<a id="hmi-ing-023"></a>
<a id="what-effects-on-nutrition-yield-sensory-quality-stability-and-waste-streams-were-measured"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-024"></a>
<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

<a id="sampling-and-testing"></a>
## Testing sheep casings for metals

<a id="hmi-ing-025"></a>
<a id="what-sampling-design-is-appropriate-for-the-ingredient-heterogeneity-lot-and-decision"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-026"></a>
<a id="which-methods-species-measurements-validation-evidence-and-reporting-limits-are-needed"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-027"></a>
<a id="what-can-a-certificate-of-analysis-or-non-detect-establish-and-what-remains-untested"></a>

Results depend on the method and its reporting limit. Reporting limits for lead were 10 µg/kg where sources stated them.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wysok B, Wojtacka J, Szczotka-Bochniarz A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Heavy Metal Contamination in Natural Sheep Casings</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Reporting limits for cadmium were 1 µg/kg where sources stated them.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wysok B, Wojtacka J, Szczotka-Bochniarz A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Heavy Metal Contamination in Natural Sheep Casings</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Reporting limits for total arsenic were 10 µg/kg where sources stated them.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wysok B, Wojtacka J, Szczotka-Bochniarz A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Heavy Metal Contamination in Natural Sheep Casings</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

A useful lot result names the form, the basis and a quantification limit well below the limit that applies.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. <a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Sheep casings FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-sheep-casings" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-sheep-casings" data-question="What heavy metals are found in sheep casings?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in sheep casings?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury in sheep casings, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wysok B, Wojtacka J, Szczotka-Bochniarz A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Heavy Metal Contamination in Natural Sheep Casings</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-origins-or-products-of-sheep-casings-measured-lowest" data-anchor="which-origins-or-products-of-sheep-casings-measured-lowest" data-question="Which origins or products of sheep casings measured lowest?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of sheep casings measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, lead across 8 groups of sheep casings ranged from 64 µg/kg (casings of New Zealand origin) to 97 µg/kg (casings of Pakistan origin); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wysok B, Wojtacka J, Szczotka-Bochniarz A · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Heavy Metal Contamination in Natural Sheep Casings</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wysok2025-heavy-metals-sheep-casings">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
